# no-unnecessary-is-valid-check

Warn when checking `isValid` on references already known to be valid.

This is the counterpart to [`require-is-valid-check`](./require-is-valid-check.md).
A reference branded as validated (e.g. `ValidPlayer`) is guaranteed valid within
the synchronous scope where it was obtained, so re-checking `isValid` there is
redundant noise.

Control-flow narrowing such as `entity instanceof Player` drops the optional
Valid\* brand from the use-site type. The rule still treats the binding as
known-valid when its **declared** type carries the brand (e.g. a
`ValidEventCallback` `damagingEntity` narrowed to `Player`).

The rule deliberately does **not** warn when the re-check is justified:

- after an `await`/`yield` on the path reaching the check (the handle may have
  been invalidated; a mutually exclusive branch that awaits and then
  returns/throws does not taint the continuation),
- when the branded reference comes from an outer scope and is reached through a
  deferred (non-synchronous) callback,
- for a `for...of` loop variable when the loop body awaits.

## ✅ Correct

```ts
// Re-check after an await is legitimate.
const player = world.getAllPlayers()[0];
await system.waitTicks(1);
if (player.isValid) player.kill();

// Plain (non-branded) references must still be checked.
function onHit(player: Player) {
  if (player.isValid) player.kill();
}
```

## ❌ Incorrect

```ts
const player = world.getAllPlayers()[0];
if (player.isValid) {
  // already valid here
  player.kill();
}

world.getAllPlayers().forEach(player => {
  if (player.isValid) player.kill(); // already valid
});

world.afterEvents.entityHitEntity.subscribe(({ damagingEntity }) => {
  if (!(damagingEntity instanceof Player)) return;
  if (!damagingEntity.isValid) return; // already valid from event brand
  damagingEntity.sendMessage('hit');
});
```

This rule requires [type information](https://typescript-eslint.io/getting-started/typed-linting).
